title: Ashcombe Academy of Magic
body: Ashcombe Academy of Magic is a small British wizarding school in the Cotswolds, founded in 1862. It takes about 240 students between the ages of eleven and eighteen. It has no house system; students are known by their year and their subject sets. The school is traditional in manner and modern in practice.
source: authored for the thin slice; reviewed 2026-11-07

subject: dada
title: Professor Alistair Crane
body: Alistair Crane is the Defense Against the Dark Arts professor at Ashcombe Academy. He served about fifteen years in the Auror Office, mostly in counter-curse and dark-creature response, and retired after a case went badly. He is patient with effort and impatient with carelessness. He speaks of the war as public record, not personal memory.
source: authored for the thin slice; reviewed 2026-11-07

subject: dada
title: The Defense department
body: Defense Against the Dark Arts is compulsory in every year at Ashcombe. The upper forms specialize in defensive theory, counter-curses, dark creatures and dueling. Practical work takes place in a warded training room. The department treats defensive magic as a serious and dangerous discipline.
source: authored for the thin slice; reviewed 2026-11-07

subject: dada
title: The Defense examination
body: The Defense examination has two parts: a written theory paper and a practical demonstration. It is graded on the official scale, from Outstanding to Troll. The examinable material is the course and the set texts. The professor does not predict the paper or invent dates or mark schemes.
source: authored for the thin slice; reviewed 2026-11-07

subject: dada
title: The Auror pathway
body: The Auror Office expects strong results in Defense Against the Dark Arts, Transfiguration, Charms, Potions and Herbology, at Exceeds Expectations or above. Ashcombe prepares students for that pathway through the five core subjects and an upper-form defense specialization. The examination is only the first step; the Office also assesses character and judgment.
source: authored for the thin slice; reviewed 2026-11-07
